families.title: Look up records
families.description: Which stored records or connections match my request? Look up, filter and summarize stored vertex and edge records, including bounded connection queries and extraction by record selectors. Path queries overlap with paths, and graph extraction overlaps with preparation; choose this family when the goal is retrieving records satisfying a request.
families.deciding_question: Which stored records or connections match my request?

families.title: Paths & reachability
families.description: How do I get from A to B, what can reach what, or in what order? Search, optimize or enumerate routes, compute reachability, or order dependencies. Bounded path queries also exist in records; choose this family when the goal is route analysis or dependency order.
families.deciding_question: How do I get from A to B, what can reach what, or in what order?

families.title: Connectivity, cuts & trees
families.description: Is it connected, where does it break, or what is the cheapest way to connect it? Find components and biconnected blocks, identify capacity bottlenecks with flow and cuts, or connect vertices and required groups with trees.
families.deciding_question: Is it connected, where does it break, or what is the cheapest way to connect it?

families.title: Cliques & dense subgraphs
families.description: Which tightly connected groups exist? Clique: every pair connected. Biclique: every cross pair connected. k-core: at least k neighbours each. k-truss: each edge in at least k−2 triangles. Densest: most edges per vertex, or the declared weighted or higher-order clique density. Quasi-clique: a minimum internal-degree fraction. These problems select subgraphs satisfying a structural definition; they do not require a partition of all vertices.

families.title: Communities & partitions
families.description: How should vertices be grouped or partitioned? Find communities, balanced partitions or signed-network group structure. Full partitions assign vertices to groups; local and overlapping communities may cover only part of the graph. Unlike dense, the organizing question is group membership or partition structure, rather than selecting a subgraph by a clique, core, truss or density definition.
families.deciding_question: How should vertices be grouped or partitioned?

families.title: Importance & influence
families.description: Which vertices matter most, or which seeds spread furthest? Measure vertex centrality, rank vertices globally or relative to chosen seeds, or select seeds for an explicitly defined spreading process.
families.deciding_question: Which vertices matter most, or which seeds spread furthest?

families.title: Similarity & comparison
families.description: How alike are two vertices or two graphs, or which link is missing? Compare network neighborhoods, score possible missing links, or compare and align graphs through edit distance, common subgraphs or vertex correspondences.
families.deciding_question: How alike are two vertices or two graphs, or which link is missing?

families.title: Counting motifs
families.description: How many small shapes (triangles, butterflies, graphlets, motifs, timed motifs) are there? Count or list the supported shapes, including updates to triangle counts and ordered temporal events. Bipartite and temporal input requirements determine eligibility, not separate families.
families.deciding_question: How many small shapes (triangles, butterflies, graphlets, motifs, timed motifs) are there?

families.title: Pattern matching & mining
families.description: Where does a given pattern occur, or which patterns are frequent? Match a supplied pattern or mine frequent subgraphs in one graph or a graph collection, using the problem's declared matching and support semantics.
families.deciding_question: Where does a given pattern occur, or which patterns are frequent?

families.title: Assignment & selection
families.description: Pick non-conflicting pairs or items, cover every edge, or colour without conflicts. Match pairs or assign workers to tasks, select independent vertices, cover connections with vertices, or assign colours under the declared conflict rules.
families.deciding_question: Pick non-conflicting pairs or items, cover every edge, or colour without conflicts.

families.title: Prepare, sample & draw
families.description: Build, clean, shrink, sample, extract or draw a graph before analysis. Resolve entities, construct or reduce graphs, sample neighborhoods or walks, and compute layouts. Graph extraction overlaps with records; choose this family when the goal is preparing a graph for subsequent analysis.
families.deciding_question: Build, clean, shrink, sample, extract or draw a graph before analysis.

families.title: Spectral & topology
families.description: Eigenvectors, smoothing signals over the graph, or shape across thresholds. Compute Laplacian eigenpairs, denoise graph signals, or track topological features through a filtration.
families.deciding_question: Eigenvectors, smoothing signals over the graph, or shape across thresholds.

families.title: Statistics & anomalies
families.description: Is this unusual compared with a baseline or a random graph? Detect graph anomalies under an explicit baseline or assess significance against a declared null-model ensemble.
families.deciding_question: Is this unusual compared with a baseline or a random graph?

families.title: Learning & embeddings
families.description: Learn from features and labels, or learn vectors for vertices or triples. Train vertex, graph or hypergraph predictors, condense training data, infer locations under a declared model, or learn node and knowledge-graph embeddings. Hypergraph inputs are an eligibility requirement, not a separate family.
families.deciding_question: Learn from features and labels, or learn vectors for vertices or triples.

problems.title: Look up entity records
problems.description: Native deterministic selection of original vertex records by typed IDs and AND field predicates. Explicit empty vertex lists select nothing. Missing fields match only exists=false; unknown field paths fail. Counts remain complete when row collections are capped.

problems.title: Filter relationship records and join endpoint attributes
problems.description: Native deterministic original-edge selection without collapsing loops or parallel events. Edge and source/target predicates use stored endpoints even for undirected input. Typed IDs, exact decimal scalar comparisons and explicit incomplete capped ports.

problems.title: Find nearby entities over selected relationships
problems.description: Native filtered hop reachability with exact distances. Directed out/in/both traversal; undirected edges traverse both ways. Parallel records do not duplicate vertices; include_seed controls the root. Original input vertex ordering and explicit collection completeness.

problems.title: Find the direct neighbors two entities share
problems.description: Native intersection of direct filtered neighbor sets, preserving the declared direction and self-loop adjacency meaning. Typed entity IDs; stable original vertex order. Complete count with explicitly capped collections.

problems.title: Find bounded connections between two entities
problems.description: Native iterative enumeration of all hop-shortest or all vertex-simple paths within max_hops. Filtered directed out/in/both traversal with parallel edge identities preserved. Source equal to target has one zero-edge path. Counts are exhaustive; capped path and membership ports are incomplete.

problems.title: Summarize recorded numeric values
problems.description: Native count, sum, average, minimum or maximum of an explicit field, grouped by a scalar field or vertex. Exact decimal rational arithmetic is authoritative; display values disclose rounding. Per-vertex edge groups include isolates and count loops once. Missing numeric/group fields fail. Stable exact-value sorting and completeness-aware result limits.

problems.title: Extract selected records as a graph
problems.description: Native vertex-induced, edge-induced or filtered-neighborhood extraction. Preserve typed IDs, original attributes, direction, weights, loop and parallel records. Edge mode retains endpoints; vertex mode retains selected isolates. Derived graph identity carries source content lineage.

problems.title: Learn vertex vectors from edge or walk context objectives
problems.description: Native second-order LINE or DeepWalk/node2vec fixed-window contexts, optimized with full-softmax cross entropy and declared L2 regularization. Weighted outgoing transitions preserve direction unless projection is requested. Explicit loop handling and summed parallel weights; every vertex receives source and context vectors. Report actual context masses, objective, gradient norm, seed and stopping reason; no global optimum or unique embedding claim.

problems.title: Learn typed directed triple scores with DistMult
problems.description: Native DistMult with mean logistic loss over declared training positives and fixed sampled corruptions, plus L2 regularization. Relations come only from the training split; duplicate triples collapse, distinct relation identities and self triples remain. Validation never affects fitting. Report entity/relation parameters, training examples and filtered head/tail ranking metrics with average ties; no unseen-relation inference.

problems.title: Train a graph-based vertex classifier or regressor
problems.description: Native simplified graph convolution: declared mean-message layers, then a trained linear softmax or scalar regression readout. Numeric vertex_features and training_labels use objects containing typed {vertex,value} rows. Disjoint train/validation/test IDs; preprocessing and loss use training labels only. Transductive unlabeled features/topology are explicit. Saved coefficients, split metrics, objective and convergence status; one self message, collapsed parallels, weights ignored.

problems.title: Train a permutation-invariant graph predictor
problems.description: Native independent per-graph mean message passing, sum/mean pooling, and trained linear softmax or scalar regression readout. Structural [one,in-degree,out-degree] or declared attribute features; empty graphs pool to zeros. graph_labels uses typed {graph,value} rows. Train-only fitted preprocessing and supervised loss, disjoint graph splits and saved model state. Weights ignored; no cross-graph edges.

problems.title: Learn vertex targets through the original hyperedge incidence
problems.description: Native hgnn-linear-v1: weighted hyperedge feature means followed by normalized vertex incidence means and a trained linear softmax/regression layer. No pairwise projection. Isolates retain features, singleton edges remain. Feature, target and split attributes are explicit; only train labels fit parameters or preprocessing. Record model state, finite predictions and metrics with split denominators. Optional model_parameters declare layers and optimizer settings.

problems.title: Propagate geographic seed locations under a geodesic objective
problems.description: Native spatial propagation by sequential discrete geodesic median coordinate descent. Minimize positive edge weight times spherical distance, restricting coordinates to seed locations in each connected component. Undirected nonnegative input, reject loops, sum parallels. Fixed seeds remain exact; seedless components remain unresolved. Haversine handles the antimeridian; report dispersion, stopping status and optional held-out geodesic errors. No supervised model or calibrated confidence claim.

problems.title: Learn synthetic graph features by matching supervised gradients
problems.description: Native gradient_matching_linear_sgc_v1 matches training softmax gradients at zero readout parameters. Learn synthetic features and fix class-balanced labels on declared edgeless adjacency; this is not graph coarsening. Original weighted SGC features use summed parallel weights plus self messages; reject original loops. Budget must cover training classes and not exceed training vertices. Train labels only, explicit transductive features/topology, new synthetic IDs. Evaluate full versus synthetic training on held-out original labels over declared seeds; report objective and utility variance.

problems.title: Rank graph entities against a declared reference
problems.description: Native structural and numeric features for vertices, original edge instances or supplied induced subgraphs. Population or explicit location/scale reference; weighted standardized L1, L2 or maximum deviation with declared minimum scale. Recompute scores, preserve zero-variance failures and disclose top-k truncation. Numerical deviation scores are not learned ground truth.

problems.title: Find candidate record pairs and resolve declared matches
problems.description: Complete native disjunctive blocking rules with equality, Unicode tokens, codepoint Levenshtein or exact numeric difference. ICU NFKC and full case folding; optional missing fields fail the predicate. Input edges are unused hints. Connected-components resolution or exact bounded minimum candidate-pair disagreement partitions; neutral noncandidates and no cross-component clusters.

problems.title: Compute minimum graph edit cost with an executable witness
problems.description: Exact bounded native partial correspondences over simple normalized directed or undirected graphs. Selected categorical vertex/edge labels; decimal rational costs. Vertex label replacement costs insertion plus deletion, edge substitution competes with deletion plus insertion. Returns normalized graphs and an ordered stable-handle script whose total is checked against the optimum. Weights and timestamps are ignored.

problems.title: Find the largest common graph by vertex count
problems.description: Exact bounded native induced matching, or label-compatible maximum vertex matching for non-induced output where isolated vertices are allowed. Preserve direction and selected categorical labels, ignore weights/timestamps. Returns a checked common graph and injective correspondence. No secondary maximum-edge objective. Explicit loop/parallel normalization.

problems.title: Aggregate vertices and edges into a weighted quotient graph
problems.description: Supplied integer partition or native greedy maximal matching; all vertices remain represented. Undirected nonnegative input, reject loops. Sum original parallel edge weights once, retain or drop intra-cluster edges, sum or mean feature vectors. Exact rational aggregates are reported separately from rounded binary64 graph values. Greedy partition has no optimality claim.

problems.title: Sample fewer edges and measure every Laplacian distortion direction
problems.description: Native effective-resistance sampling with replacement, exact rational draw normalization and importance reweighting. LAPACK grounded solves and all generalized eigenvalues measure numerical distortion; requested epsilon must pass. Explicit weighted undirected simple input, no loops/parallels. Preserve original IDs/attributes. Identity shortcut when budget covers positive edges, zero-weight edges removed. No probabilistic approximation guarantee is claimed.

problems.title: Mine patterns shared across graph transactions
problems.description: Exact bounded native enumeration of simple labeled directed or undirected patterns, including disconnected and isolated vertices. Support counts transactions once. Native lexicographic canonicalization has its own stable pattern IDs. Positive support fraction uses exact decimal comparison. Explicit loop and parallel policies; no Python runtime.

problems.title: Mine frequent labeled patterns within a graph
problems.description: Exact connected undirected patterns including single vertices. Minimum-image support is the smallest host image-set size over all injective embeddings. Every vertex needs the selected label or type. Reject loops; explicit parallel collapse. Native canonical IDs, bounded enumeration and complete counts; count mode does not materialize patterns.

problems.title: Count graph patterns with ordered edge events
problems.description: Exact native structural matching and injective event assignments. Rational UTC timestamps, acyclic partial order, inclusive duration limit, optional temporal inducedness and typed predicates. Event tuples in query-edge input order identify occurrences. Counts and vertex participation remain complete when instance lists are capped.

problems.title: Connect nearby feature vectors
problems.description: Native exhaustive pairwise Euclidean, squared Euclidean or cosine distances with self-exclusion and input-order tie breaking. Directed, union or mutual symmetrization. Cosine rejects zero vectors. Exact neighbor search under numerical distances even when approximate is requested; preserves typed vector IDs.

problems.title: Partition hyperedges directly with bounded vertex weights
problems.description: Exact native enumeration of nonempty parts, optimizing weighted cut-net or connectivity-minus-one without graph projection. Exact rational vertex and hyperedge weights, decimal imbalance tolerance and upper part-weight bound. Certified infeasibility when no partition qualifies; exponential search obeys work budgets.

problems.title: Find matches for a supplied graph pattern
problems.description: Exact native induced or non-induced injective matching, preserving direction, loops and parallel multiplicities. Declarative typed vertex and edge predicates; distinct query edges must match distinct data edges. Capped mapping collections are explicitly incomplete.

problems.title: Count supplied connected motifs
problems.description: Exact structural embeddings with explicit occurrence identity: all mappings or unique vertex-set and image-edge classes. Preserve direction; simple projections discard loops, duplicate edges and weights. Non-induced motifs on the same vertex set can be distinct instances. Counts remain complete when lists are capped.

problems.title: Count connected induced graph shapes and vertex roles
problems.description: Native isomorphism classification against the complete connected undirected graph atlas for sizes two through seven. Static atlas IDs and exact automorphism orbits are embedded; Python is not required. Discard loops and duplicate edges, ignore weights. Counts and optional orbit participation stay complete when memberships are capped.

problems.title: Connect representatives of every required group
problems.description: Exact bounded vertex-subset optimization with a minimum spanning tree for each feasible induced subgraph. Covers every group and required vertex, allowing overlapping representatives. Undirected nonnegative weighted input, loops removed, cheapest original parallel edge retained. Reports exact rational cost or certified infeasibility.

backends.execution: original native CUDA adapter; runtime profile and output checks

gpu_limitations: GPU4GST: explicit nonnegative integer weights; at most 16 groups including required singleton vertices; native optimum verification

problems.title: Align two graphs while conserving edges and supplied similarities
problems.description: Exact bounded global injective assignment covering every vertex of the smaller graph. Maximize topology_weight times conserved edge value plus pair priors. Direction must match. Drop loops and collapse unweighted or sum nonnegative weighted parallel edges. Weighted conservation is the minimum of paired normalized edge weights.

problems.title: Choose seeds that maximize expected diffusion
problems.description: Exact native IC/LT optimization, or explicitly requested SuperFuser independent-cascade heuristic with holdout spread estimation. The heuristic does not certify optimality or an approximation guarantee.

backends.execution: original native CUDA adapter; runtime profile and output checks

gpu_limitations: SuperFuser: solution_quality=heuristic, independent_cascade, explicit probabilities, sample_count a multiple of 32 in [32,65536]

problems.title: Compare a statistic with a random graph ensemble
problems.description: Uniform G(n,m), or uniform stub pairing conditioned on simplicity and exact degree invariants. Dense fixed-degree graphs use complement sampling. Preserve direction, discard loops and collapse duplicates. Statistics: triangles, directed triangles, k-cliques, density or a supplied-partition modularity. Report every sample, population standard deviation and declared empirical tail; no hidden pseudocount.

problems.title: Track connected components and holes across edge thresholds
problems.description: Exact sparse boundary reduction of a flag complex over a declared prime field. Vertices start at zero; include cofaces needed to compute deaths in requested dimensions. Undirected input; reject loops, require nonnegative weights, keep minimum parallel filtration. Optional cutoff marks unpaired intervals right-censored.

problems.title: Find a community around required seeds
problems.description: Heuristic personalized-PageRank degree-normalized sweep with required seeds first. Returns the lowest defined weighted conductance among feasible prefixes. Exact cut/volume recomputation, no global-optimum claim. Undirected input; reject loops, sum nonnegative parallel weights. If all conductance denominators vanish, return the seeds.

problems.title: Compute a force-directed network drawing
problems.description: Native Fruchterman-Reingold iterations in two or three dimensions. Explicit 0.01 distance regularization, linear cooling from one tenth of the maximum coordinate span, no final rescaling. Recompute matching potential and uncooled force residual; no drawing optimality claim. Project direction, drop loops, collapse unweighted or sum weighted parallels.

problems.title: Compute Laplacian eigenvalues and eigenvectors
problems.description: Native LAPACK symmetric eigensolver with independently recomputed absolute residual and orthogonality checks. Combinatorial or symmetric-normalized Laplacian, including isolates. Undirected input; reject loops and negative weights, sum parallel weights. Dense solver uses work budgets; no iteration parameter.

problems.title: Smooth noisy measurements over a graph
problems.description: Minimize half squared signal error plus Laplacian quadratic, weighted total variation, or explicit graph-trend penalty. Native positive-definite solve or accelerated feasible-dual optimization; tolerance bounds objective gap, with a separate L2 solution-error bound. Undirected input, no loops, nonnegative summed parallel weights.

problems.title: Compare vertices by the similarity of their neighbors
problems.description: Native float64 SimRank fixed-point iteration with a recomputed contraction error bound. Incoming or undirected-projection neighborhoods; drop loops and duplicates, ignore weights. Single-source output excludes itself. Top-k ports explicitly disclose omitted pairs.

problems.title: Find the greatest bottleneck capacity from a source
problems.description: Exact max-min capacities with a predecessor witness, preserving direction. Every edge needs nonnegative capacity; loops discarded and largest parallel capacity wins. Zero is reachable. Source infinity and unreachable nulls have distinct flags.

problems.title: Find the highest-cost paths through a DAG
problems.description: Exact rational k-best DAG paths, retaining parallel edge identities and negative weights. Omitted sources and sinks select zero-in/out-degree vertices. A zero-edge path is included when a source is also a sink. Finishing top-k does not imply the path collection is exhaustive.

problems.title: Find earliest arrivals or fastest journeys through timed events
problems.description: Exact rational time-expanded shortest paths. Directed event input; every edge needs a timestamp and nonnegative duration attribute. Waiting is allowed. Fastest duration excludes waiting before initial departure. Inclusive ready time and deadline preserve distinct parallel events.

problems.title: Enumerate bounded simple paths or cycles
problems.description: Exact directed simple edge paths and cycles up to max_hops. Drop loops; collapse to first parallel edge or retain identities. Optional strict chronological order applies after canonical cycle rotation. A result cap retains the shortest sequences while the total count remains exhaustive.

problems.title: Divide a network into communities
problems.description: Undirected modularity or constant Potts objective. Exact mode enumerates partitions with rational objectives; heuristic mode uses seeded positive-gain vertex moves and makes no global-optimum claim. Drop loops and collapse unweighted or sum weighted parallel edges. CPM is internal edge weight minus resolution times within-part vertex pairs.

problems.title: Split a graph into balanced groups with few crossing edges
problems.description: Exact bounded partition search with nonempty parts and both lower and upper balance limits. Undirected input, nonnegative edge weights, loop removal and duplicate collapse or weighted sum. Normalized cut sums each part boundary divided by its declared balance size. Decimal-rational imbalance tolerance; exact objective and infeasibility certificates.

problems.title: Check balance or minimize frustrated connections
problems.description: Exact signed parity balance test and bounded rational frustration minimization. Every edge type is positive or negative. Undirected input; drop loops, reject contradictory parallel signs and collapse unweighted or sum weighted parallels. Zero-cost violations still make the network structurally unbalanced.

problems.title: Find the region with the most edges or cliques per vertex
problems.description: Exact induced k-clique count divided by vertex count. Weighted density is defined for clique_order=2, summing parallel weights. Undirected input; loops discarded. Native rational maximum-weight closure for minimum_vertices=1; bounded exhaustive cardinality search otherwise.

problems.title: Find exactly k vertices with the greatest internal edge value
problems.description: Exact bounded cardinality search. Sum parallel nonnegative weights, discard loops, require undirected input. An approximate request receives the stronger exact result when search completes.

problems.title: Find groups meeting a minimum internal-degree fraction
problems.description: Exact gamma quasi-cliques on an undirected simple projection. Thresholds use decimal-rational gamma; maximality is relative to all qualifying sets within the size bounds. Search is bounded by work and output budgets.

problems.description: Exact inclusion-maximal bicliques with nonempty sides. Supply both disjoint partitions covering every vertex, or omit both to use every vertex's attributes.side=left|right. Undirected input; loops discarded and duplicate edges collapsed. Capped memberships are marked incomplete.

problems.description: Exact 2-by-2 biclique counts, participation and alpha/beta cores. Every vertex requires attributes.side=left|right. Reject directed input, loops and same-side edges; collapse duplicates. Core thresholds explicitly use degree or butterfly participation.

problems.description: Exact reflexive reachability: every vertex reaches itself by a zero-length path. Preserve graph direction, ignore weights, loops and duplicates. Count-only closure has a complete scalar and incomplete pair-list port.

problems.title: Find overlapping tightly connected groups
problems.description: Exact k-clique percolation. Undirected simple projection; discard loops and duplicates. Communities can overlap. Unassigned vertices are outside all percolation communities before minimum-size display filtering.

problems.title: Connections within a number of steps
problems.description: Minimum hop distances with explicit independent or nearest-source searches. Preserve direction; discard loops and collapse duplicate arcs; weights are ignored. IDs are signed int64 or strings.

problems.title: Count or list triangles
problems.description: Count three-vertex cliques of an undirected graph. Discard loops and collapse duplicate edges; weights are ignored. GPU enumeration uses native CPU materialization with count verification.

problems.title: Shortest weighted paths from one vertex
problems.description: Nonnegative lengths; preserve direction, drop loops and keep minimum parallel length. CPU returns exact rational costs over admitted binary64 weights; GPU returns float64 costs. Cutoff is inclusive.

problems.title: Shortest paths between selected vertex sets
problems.description: Selected origins and destinations, or all vertices for null. Nonnegative lengths, minimum parallel length and preserved direction; CPU exact costs and GPU float64 costs.
gpu_limitations: Path cost bounds must fit float64; integral costs beyond 2^53 require CPU

problems.title: Minimum or maximum spanning forest
problems.description: Undirected weighted forests with isolates retained. Negative lengths are allowed. Keep minimum or maximum parallel weights according to the objective; discard loops.

problems.title: Connected vertex groups
problems.description: Weak or strong connectivity. Weak mode uses an undirected projection; strong mode preserves direction. Loops, duplicate edges and weights do not affect membership.

problems.title: Extract a graph around selected vertices
problems.description: Exact induced or ego subgraph, preserving typed IDs, edge instances and properties. Ego radius includes all vertices within that distance. problems.title: Find the highest-value non-conflicting pairs
problems.description: Exact maximum-weight matching on an undirected graph, with no cardinality constraint. Require nonnegative weights; discard loops and keep the largest parallel weight. Preserve selected original edge IDs and return exact rational totals over admitted binary64 weights. Zero-weight edges may be omitted.

problems.title: Match items on two sides by count, value or cost
